title: Make history pagination deterministic when posting timestamps tie
prompt:
Give history queries a deterministic tie-breaker; work on the assigned branch you are on. Edit only packages/ledger/src/index.ts as production code, specifically getHistory. packages/ledger/src/index.ts:174-176 filters by account, order only by created_at descending, and then apply an offset range. sql/001_schema.sql:58 defines a unique posting id, while line 62 defaults posting timestamps to NOW(), so equal timestamps are allowed. A local query-stub reproduction executed the actual getHistory twice using two permitted orders of tied rows and returned the same transaction on consecutive one-entry pages. This demonstrates an ordering gap, not a claim that a live database was queried.

Add a secondary descending order on the posting id before applying range. Preserve newest-first ordering, account filtering, offset/limit semantics, selected data, error handling, and response mapping. Do not sort after pagination or change transaction identifiers. This only stabilizes ties for a fixed dataset; cursor pagination and concurrent insertion behavior are outside scope. No schema or index migration is needed.

Add tests/ledger/history-stable-order.test.mjs. Execute the real function with a read-only query stub that honors the requested ordering over several equal-timestamp rows, permutes their incoming order between calls, and applies range last. Verify repeated and adjacent pages are deterministic without duplicate or omitted fixtures, mixed timestamps remain newest-first, and account filtering persists. Run node --test tests/ledger/history-stable-order.test.mjs and node --test tests/security/*.test.mjs. No credentials, payments, sends, deployments, migrations, auth, workflows or package.json changes. Do not commit or push.
